questions: Do all cars have the same speed, or can speeds vary between cars?
Are the cars initially positioned such that each left-to-right car has a unique corresponding right-to-left car at the same starting distance from some origin?
Do we count encounters that occur exactly when cars pass through each other's positions, or only when they occupy overlapping positions for nonzero time?
Are the two sets of cars initially interleaved along the road, or are all left-to-right cars to the left of all right-to-left cars initially?
Is 'very far from each other' meant to imply that initially no left-to-right car is to the right of any right-to-left car?
Should we count multiple encounters between the same pair of cars if they pass through each other more than once?
Are the cars considered to have zero size (points) or nonzero length?
Does 'encounter' require the cars to be at the same position at the same time, or merely pass within some proximity threshold?
